newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine sugar beet harvest at 11.18 mln T-ministry.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine sugar beet harvest at 11.18 mln T-ministry.

text.p: Ukraine has harvested 11.18 million tonnes of sugar beets, down from 17.50 million tonnes at this time last year, a senior Agriculture Ministry spokesman said on Monday.
Valentyn Tymoshenko told Reuters that sugar beet yields were down to 20.0 tonnes per hectare from last year's 21.9 tonnes.
The beet harvest was proceeding more slowly this year, with 560,000 hectares harvested, compared to 801,000 hectares at this time in 1995.

This year Ukraine, which sowed 1.306 million hectares to sugar beets, left them in the ground for two weeks longer than usual to allow them to grow larger, after dry conditions in spring delayed planting by two weeks.
Ukrainian Agriculture Minister Anatoly Khorishko predicted last week that this year's total harvest would be a poor 26 million tonnes, against 30 million tonnes in 1995.
Anatoly Prokopenko, the deputy head of the Weather Forecasting Centre, told Reuters that warm and dry weather expected through October would favour harvest conditions.
"We have predicted no rain in most parts of our country in the next few weeks and a slight slip in temperatures, especially at night," Prokopenko said.
"Right now every second counts, so this is good news for beet harvesting farmers."
Khorishko also said refined sugar output from this year's beet harvest would be at 3.2 million tonnes, compared to 3.485 million tonnes last year.
Government officials have blamed drought at the beginning of the summer, equipment breakdowns and chronic fuel shortages for this year's delays in the sugar beet campaign.
